newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 17.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 17.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- The Parliament has set up an investigative committee to unveil who is politically responsible for the privatisation scandal over irregular paymnents to an advisor.

- The opposition Smallholders' Party (FKGP) said Gabor Kuncze, Minister of Home Affairs is just as responsible for the privatisation scandal than Tamas Suchman who had been dismissed from the post of minister of industry and trade.
- The opposition party Fidesz said it will "take radical steps" if the parties of the ruling coalition are proved to have got involved in the privatisation scandal.
- The State Audit Office said the state's interests were not vindicated sufficiently in the privatisation of the national telephone services monopoly Matav.
- The Government Supervisory Office started to examine the state privatisation agency APV's contracts with advisors.
